text.en: Asha saw a sunflower turning its face to the Sun and a touch-me-not plant closing its leaves. "Plants respond too!" she said.

A growth movement whose direction depends on the direction of the stimulus is called tropism, as in phototropism towards light, geotropism towards gravity and hydrotropism towards water. A non-directional response to a stimulus, like the closing of touch-me-not leaves, is a nastic movement.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants prepare their food. It needs sunlight, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide and water, and it gives out oxygen. The glucose made is the food of the plant.
Transpiration is the loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of the plant, mainly through stomata on the leaf. Stomata also exchange gases. Transpiration pulls water up the plant and cools the leaf.

problem.en: What four things does photosynthesis need?

text.en: They need chlorophyll, carbon dioxide and water.
So: sunlight, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide and water.

prompt.en: A friend says Nastic movements depend on the direction of the stimulus. How will you reply?

points.en: Transpiration is loss of water vapour.
